index.content: Character creation follows numbered steps: roll Stats (2d10+25 each), roll Saves (2d10+10 each), choose a class, roll Health (1d10+10), start Stress at 2, note the class Trauma Response, choose Skills, and roll Loadout, Trinket, and Patch. Starting Credits are 2d10x10.
Roll 2 ten-sided dice (2d10), add them together, then add 25. Record the result for each of the four Stats: Strength, Speed, Intellect, and Combat. A Stat of 36 is average.

Roll 2 ten-sided dice (2d10), add them together, then add 10. Record the result for each of the three Saves: Sanity, Fear, and Body. Saves represent resistance and reaction to different kinds of trauma and danger.

There are four classes: Marines (+10 Combat, +10 Body Save, +20 Fear Save, +1 Max Wounds), Androids (+20 Intellect, -10 to 1 Stat, +60 Fear Save, +1 Max Wounds), Scientists (+10 Intellect, +5 to 1 Stat, +30 Sanity Save), and Teamsters (+5 to all Stats, +10 to all Saves). Each has a distinct Trauma Response.
Roll 1 ten-sided die (1d10) then add 10. Record the result for Maximum Health. Characters start at their Maximum Health with zero Wounds.
Current Stress and Minimum Stress both start at 2.

Each class deals with Stress and Panic differently. Marine: whenever you Panic, every Close friendly player must make a Fear Save. Android: Fear Saves made by Close friendly players are at Disadvantage. Scientist: whenever you fail a Sanity Save, all Close friendly players gain 1 Stress. Teamster: once per session you may take Advantage on a Panic Check.
Each class comes preloaded with relevant Skills. To choose a Skill you must have at least one prerequisite Skill first. Trained Skills grant +10, Expert Skills +15, and Master Skills +20.
Roll for a Loadout based on your class (1d10 on the class Loadout table), then roll for a Trinket and a Patch on the d100 tables. Finally, roll 2d10 and multiply by 10 for starting Credits.
Roll 1d100 less than or equal to your Strength, Speed, Intellect, or Combat to accomplish a task; otherwise fail and gain 1 Stress. A roll of 90-99 is always considered a failure.
Roll 1d100 less than or equal to your Sanity, Fear, or Body to avoid danger; otherwise fail and gain 1 Stress. A roll of 90-99 is always considered a failure.
If a character has a Skill relevant to the task, add its Skill Bonus to the Stat before rolling a Stat Check. Trained Skills grant +10, Expert Skills +15, and Master Skills +20.
Advantage [+] means roll twice and take the best result; Disadvantage [-] means roll twice and take the worst result.
Whenever you roll doubles on 1d100, the result is special. A successful double is a Critical Success; a failed double is a Critical Failure that forces a Panic Check.

To make a Panic Check, roll the Panic Die (1d20) and attempt to roll greater than your current Stress. If you roll less than or equal to your current Stress you fail, and you look up your result on the Panic Table.

Make a Panic Check on any Critical Failure on a Stat Check or Save, watching another crewmember die, witnessing multiple crewmembers Panic, a Ship Critical Failure, encountering a horrifying entity for the first time, or when the Warden deems appropriate.
Severe Panic Table results leave lasting Conditions that affect the character until treated via Medical Care.
Make a Combat Check. If successful, roll the weapon's Damage and subtract it from the enemy's Health. If you fail, the situation gets worse and you gain 1 Stress.

When taking Damage, subtract it from Health. If Health reaches zero, gain a Wound and roll on the Wounds Table, then reset Health to Maximum minus carryover damage. Once you suffer your Maximum Wounds, make a Death Save.

Characters ignore all Damage less than their armor's Armor Points (AP). If they take Damage greater than or equal to their AP in one hit, armor is destroyed and remaining Damage carries over. Anti-Armor (AA) weapons ignore and destroy armor. Damage Reduction (DR) always reduces incoming Damage by the stated amount.
Cover provides protection and can be destroyed when dealt Damage greater than or equal to its AP. Insignificant Cover AP 5, Light Cover AP 10, Heavy Cover DR 5 AP 20.
When gaining a Wound, roll 1d10 on the Wounds Table according to Damage type: Blunt Force, Bleeding, Gunshot, Fire & Explosives, or Gore & Massive. Severity ranges from Flesh Wound to Fatal Injury.

When death seems imminent, the Warden makes a Death Save by rolling 1d10 in secret. The Death Table: 00 unconscious (wake in 2d10 min, -1d5 Max Health), 01-02 unconscious and dying, 03-04 comatose, 05-09 dead.
Range is tracked in Range Bands: Adjacent (less than 1m), Close Range (5-10m), Long Range (20-100m), and Extreme Range (more than 100m).
At a safe Port, pay Shore Leave costs and make a Sanity Save to convert accumulated Stress into improved Saves. Every point of Stress converted improves any Save by one.
Contractors are hireable NPCs with Salary, Combat, Instinct, and Max Wounds. Contractors who survive a job and are paid in full increase their Loyalty by 1.

A Horror includes a Transgression that awakens it, Omens of its arrival, its Manifestation, a Banishment that defeats it, and its effects as it Slumbers. Roll on the Horrors d100 table to generate one.

The TOMBS cycle gives players a choice to Survive the nightmare, Solve the mystery, or Save the day. Obstacles include Violent Encounters, Psychological Trauma, Environmental Hazards, Social Pressures, and Resource Scarcity.

Puzzles are built from components such as Alarm, Connect the Dots, Dilemma, Guardian, Lock & Key, Riddle, Sequence, and Trap. A good puzzle allows multiple solutions and lets the game continue if left unsolved.
Evidence comes in three types (Testimonial, Physical, Documentary) and each generates Leads pointing to a person, place, or thing. Reveal facts, not conclusions; show the lock before the key.

The Setting Table offers 10 self-contained locations: Space Station, Aboard Your Own Ship, Military Outpost, Prison Complex, Derelict Spacecraft, Religious Compound, Mining Colony, Research Facility, Underwater Base, and Mothership.

Ten starting scenarios include Explore the Unknown, Investigate a Strange Rumor, Salvage a Derelict Ship, Exterminate an Otherworldly Threat, Visit an Offworld Colony, Undertake a Dangerous Mission, Survive a Colossal Disaster, Respond to a Distress Signal, Transport Precious Cargo, and Make Contact with the Beyond.

stats.name: Stats
stats.description: Four Stats represent how well a character acts under extreme pressure: Strength, Speed, Intellect, and Combat. Roll 2d10, add together, then add 25 for each Stat. A Stat of 36 is average.

strength.name: Strength
strength.description: Physical power, muscle, and brawn. Key Stat for melee combat, lifting, and feats of physical force.

speed.name: Speed
speed.description: Agility, reflexes, and dexterity. Key Stat for dodging, sprinting, and fine motor tasks.

intellect.name: Intellect
intellect.description: Reasoning, knowledge, and technical aptitude. Key Stat for hacking, research, and scientific tasks.

combat.name: Combat
combat.description: Fighting skill and lethality under fire. Key Stat for attacking with weapons.

saves.name: Saves
saves.description: Three Saves represent how resistant and reactive a character is to trauma and danger: Sanity, Fear, and Body. Roll 2d10, add together, then add 10 for each Save.

sanity_save.name: Sanity Save
sanity_save.description: Rolled against attacks on reason — things that do not make sense, cosmic horror, and mental dissonance.

fear_save.name: Fear Save
fear_save.description: Rolled against attacks on emotion — visceral, guttural terror and gut reactions such as loneliness or rage.

body_save.name: Body Save
body_save.description: Rolled against physical hazards — poison, disease, radiation, explosions, and drowning.

health.name: Health
health.description: Roll 1d10 then add 10 for Maximum Health. Characters start at Maximum Health with zero Wounds. When Health falls below zero, the character suffers a Wound, then Health resets to Maximum minus any carryover damage.

wounds.name: Wounds
wounds.description: A limited number of Wounds a character can suffer before dying. Each class has a different starting Maximum Wounds. When a character reaches zero Health they gain a Wound and roll on the Wounds Table.

stress.name: Stress
stress.description: A character's current Stress and Minimum Stress both start at 2. Stress makes characters more likely to Panic, but is also needed to improve Saves via Shore Leave.

panic_check.name: Panic Check
panic_check.description: Determines whether a character keeps their cool under extreme pressure. Roll the Panic Die (1d20) and attempt to roll GREATER than current Stress. If you roll less than or equal to current Stress, you fail and look up the result on the Panic Table.

armor_points.name: Armor Points
armor_points.description: Characters ignore all Damage less than their armor's Armor Points. If they take Damage greater than or equal to their AP in one hit, the armor is destroyed and remaining Damage carries over.

damage_reduction.name: Damage Reduction
damage_reduction.description: Always reduces incoming Damage by the stated amount, even if armor is destroyed or the weapon has Anti-Armor. Damage Reduction occurs first, before any Armor.

anti_armor.name: Anti-Armor
anti_armor.description: Weapons with Anti-Armor ignore and destroy armor whenever they hit.

advantage.name: Advantage
advantage.description: Represented by [+] on a roll. Roll the dice twice and take the best result.

disadvantage.name: Disadvantage
disadvantage.description: Represented by [-] on a roll. Roll the dice twice and take the worst result.

critical_success.name: Critical Success
critical_success.description: Whenever you roll doubles on 1d100 that succeed, it is a Critical Success and something very good happens.

critical_failure.name: Critical Failure
critical_failure.description: Whenever you roll doubles on 1d100 that fail, it is a Critical Failure, something bad happens, and you must make a Panic Check.

skills.name: Skills
skills.description: Skills help characters perform better at challenges. Each class comes preloaded with relevant Skills. To take a Master or Expert Skill you must first take at least one prerequisite Skill.

conditions.name: Conditions
conditions.description: Severe Panic Table results leave lasting impressions called Conditions, which affect the character until treated via Medical Care.

range_bands.name: Range Bands
range_bands.description: Distance is tracked abstractly in Range Bands: Adjacent, Close Range, Long Range, and Extreme Range.

credits.name: Credits
credits.description: The primary currency in Mothership. Roll 2d10 and multiply by 10 for starting Credits (2d10x10cr) in addition to a Starting Loadout.

warden.name: Warden
warden.description: The Warden prepares and runs the scenario, adjudicates rules, and plays all non-player characters. The horror framework includes a Transgression, Omens, Manifestation, Banishment, and Slumber.

stat_check.name: Stat Check
stat_check.formula: Roll 1d100 less than or equal to the relevant Stat (plus any Skill bonus)
stat_check.description: Roll 1d100 and attempt to roll under the relevant Stat (Strength, Speed, Intellect, or Combat). Success accomplishes the task; failure gains 1 Stress. A roll of 90-99 always fails.

save.name: Save
save.formula: Roll 1d100 less than or equal to the relevant Save
save.description: Saves are reactions rolled to avoid mental, emotional, and physical danger. Roll 1d100 and attempt to roll under Sanity, Fear, or Body. Failure gains 1 Stress. A roll of 90-99 always fails.

attack.name: Attack
attack.formula: Make a Combat Check; on success roll weapon Damage
attack.description: Make a Combat Check. If successful, roll the weapon's Damage and subtract it from the enemy's Health. If you fail, the situation gets worse and you gain 1 Stress.

panic_check_action.name: Panic Check
panic_check_action.description: Roll the Panic Die (1d20) and attempt to roll GREATER than current Stress. If you roll less than or equal to current Stress, you fail and look up the result on the Panic Table.

death_save.name: Death Save
death_save.description: When you reach your Maximum Wounds, the Warden makes a Death Save by rolling 1d10 in secret and looking it up on the Death Table.

character_generation.name: Character Generation
character_generation.description: Generate Stats (2d10+25 each), Saves (2d10+10 each), Health (1d10+10), Stress (starts at 2), and Credits (2d10x10).

wound_roll.name: Wound Roll
wound_roll.formula: Roll 1d10 on the Wounds Table according to Damage type
wound_roll.description: When gaining a Wound, roll 1d10 on the Wounds Table according to the type of Damage: Blunt Force, Bleeding, Gunshot, Fire & Explosives, or Gore & Massive.

core_mechanic.name: Core Mechanic
core_mechanic.description: Mothership uses a d100 roll-under mechanic. To attempt an action with a chance of failure, roll 1d100 and attempt to roll LESS THAN OR EQUAL TO the relevant Stat (for Stat Checks) or Save (for Saves). A roll of 90-99 always fails regardless of the target number. If you roll doubles, the result is a Critical: a successful double is a Critical Success, a failed double is a Critical Failure that forces a Panic Check. Skills add their bonus (+10 Trained, +15 Expert, +20 Master) to the Stat before the roll.
steps: Compare to the relevant Stat or Save
Roll under or equal to succeed; 90-99 always fails
Rolling doubles is a Critical (success or failure)

panic_mechanic.name: Panic Mechanic
panic_mechanic.description: Stress, Damage, and emotional wear bring characters to their breaking point. To determine if a character keeps their cool, roll the Panic Die (1d20) greater than current Stress. Failure means the character Panics and looks up a result on the Panic Table (01-20), which may impose lasting Conditions.
steps: Roll greater than current Stress to avoid Panic
On failure, look up the result on the Panic Table

player.name: Player
player.description: Controls a crewmember trying to survive in the most inhospitable environment in the universe: outer space. Players ask questions, roll dice, make Stat Checks and Saves, and drive the story through their character's actions.

warden.name: Warden
warden.description: The Warden prepares and narrates the scenario, adjudicates the rules, calls for Stat Checks, Saves, and Panic Checks, and plays all non-player characters and Horrors. The Warden builds Horror from a Transgression, Omens, Manifestation, Banishment, and Slumber.

player_basics.text: You can attempt anything, but when the price for failure is high, the Warden calls for a Stat Check (1d100 against Strength, Speed, Intellect, or Combat). Saves (Sanity, Fear, Body) are reactions rolled to avoid danger. Failing either gains Stress. Rolling doubles is a Critical: successes are very good, failures force a Panic Check.

warden_advice.text: A good Horror includes a Transgression that awakens it, Omens of its arrival, its Manifestation, a Banishment that defeats it, and its effects as it Slumbers. Frame obstacles as a choice to Survive the nightmare, Solve the mystery, or Save the day. Keep resources scarce and use violent encounters sparingly and brutally.

narrative_tone.text: Mothership is a sci-fi horror game for mature audiences. Characters die frequently; it is a horror game about survival, economic pressure, and fear. The Warden should make crewmembers feel vulnerable, keep tension high, and let failure cascade but always leave a path forward.

trained_skills.name: Trained Skills
trained_skills.description: Linguistics, Zoology, Field Medicine, Botany, Ecology, Geology, Industrial Equipment, Jury-Rigging, Chemistry, Computers, Zero-G, Mathematics, Art, Archaeology, Theology, Wilderness Survival, Military Training, Rimwise, Athletics, and others. Trained Skills grant +10 bonus.

expert_skills.name: Expert Skills
expert_skills.description: Psychology, Pathology, Surgery, Asteroid Mining, Hacking, Piloting, Physics, Mysticism, Firearms, Hand-to-Hand Combat, and others. Expert Skills grant +15 bonus and require a prerequisite Trained Skill.

master_skills.name: Master Skills
master_skills.description: Sophontology, Exobiology, Planetology, Robotics, Engineering, Cybernetics, Pharmacology, Artificial Intelligence, Hyperspace, Xenoesotericism, Command, and others. Master Skills grant +20 bonus and require prerequisite Expert Skills.

tools.name: search_rules
tools.title: Search Rules
tools.description: Search the Mothership ruleset for a term or phrase across all indexed sections. Use when: the exact section, entry, or term is unknown. Do NOT use when: the entity type is known — use the matching lookup_<type> tool for a canonical result. Mutation class: read-only — reads the bound ruleset's indexed data only; no state change, no audit entry, and no badge change. Returns: ranked matching entries with source anchors, or [ERROR] [NOT_FOUND] when nothing matches.

query.description: Term or phrase to search for.

tools.name: lookup_concept
tools.title: Look Up Concept
tools.description: Look up a named Mothership ruleset concept (stat, save, health, stress, panic, armor, skill, condition). Use when: resolving a rules question about a core concept by name. Do NOT use when: the exact name is unknown — use search_rules; or when rolling — use roll_dice. Mutation class: read-only — reads the bound ruleset's indexed data only; no state change, no audit entry, and no badge change. Returns: the concept entry with its source anchor, or [ERROR] [NOT_FOUND] with a 'Did you mean?' hint and the valid names.

tools.name: lookup_class
tools.title: Look Up Class
tools.description: Look up a Mothership class (Marine, Android, Scientist, Teamster) and its stat/save adjustments, skills, and trauma response. Use when: resolving a class at character creation. Do NOT use when: the class name is unknown — use search_rules. Mutation class: read-only — reads the bound ruleset's indexed data only; no state change, no audit entry, and no badge change. Returns: the class entry with its source anchor, or [ERROR] [NOT_FOUND] with a 'Did you mean?' hint and the valid names.

tools.name: lookup_action
tools.title: Look Up Action
tools.description: Look up a resolution mechanic (stat check, save, attack, panic check, death save, wound roll). Use when: resolving how a specific roll type works. Do NOT use when: rolling — use roll_dice; or when the mechanic name is unknown — use search_rules. Mutation class: read-only — reads the bound ruleset's indexed data only; no state change, no audit entry, and no badge change. Returns: the action entry with its source anchor, or [ERROR] [NOT_FOUND] with a 'Did you mean?' hint and the valid names.

tools.name: lookup_table
tools.title: Look Up Table
tools.description: Look up an indexed Mothership table (panic, death, contractors, horrors generator, setting, cover, shore leave, range bands, skill bonuses, scenarios). Use when: resolving a fixed reference or generation table. Do NOT use when: searching for a concept — use lookup_concept; or when rolling dice — use roll_dice. Mutation class: read-only — reads the bound ruleset's indexed data only; no state change, no audit entry, and no badge change. Returns: the table's rows, or [ERROR] [NOT_FOUND] on an unknown table name.

tools.name: roll_dice
tools.title: Roll Dice
tools.description: Roll dice in standard notation (NdM[+|-X], e.g. '1d100', '2d10', '1d20', '1d10+10'). Use when: making a stat check, save, panic check, or damage roll. Do NOT use when: looking up how a check works — use lookup_action. Mutation class: read-only — draws from the session's deterministic RNG and no persistence; no state change, no audit entry, and no badge change. Returns: the total, per-die breakdown, and modifier, or [ERROR] [INVALID_INPUT] on malformed notation.

tools.name: core_mechanic
tools.title: Core Mechanic
tools.description: Return the Mothership core resolution mechanic (d100 roll-under vs Stat/Save). Use when: a player asks how a stat check or save resolves. Do NOT use when: rolling — use roll_dice. Mutation class: read-only — returns rules text only; no state, audit, or badge change. Returns: the core-mechanic text.

tools.name: lookup_skill
tools.title: Look Up Skill
tools.description: Look up a Skill tier (trained, expert, master) and its bonus. Use when: resolving a skill tier's bonus. Do NOT use when: the tier name is unknown — use search_rules; or when looking up a class — use lookup_class. Mutation class: read-only — reads the bound ruleset's indexed data only; no state change, no audit entry, and no badge change. Returns: the skill tier entry with its source anchor, or [ERROR] [NOT_FOUND] with a 'Did you mean?' hint and the valid names.

prompts.name: mothership_intro
prompts.title: Mothership — Introduction
prompts.text: Welcome to Mothership, the sci-fi horror RPG of survival in outer space. Roll a d100 against your Stats (Strength, Speed, Intellect, Combat) and Saves (Sanity, Fear, Body) — roll under to succeed. Failing a Check or Save gains Stress, and when Stress mounts you risk Panicking on the Panic Die (1d20). Create a crewmember by rolling Stats (2d10+25), Saves (2d10+10), Health (1d10+10), choosing a class (Marine, Android, Scientist, or Teamster), and selecting Skills.

prompts.name: mothership_session_zero
prompts.title: Mothership — Session Zero
prompts.text: Work with your Warden to establish the scenario and tone. Roll Stats (2d10+25 each), Saves (2d10+10 each), Health (1d10+10), and starting Credits (2d10x10). Choose a class and record its Stat/Save adjustments, starting Skills, and Trauma Response. Roll your Loadout, Trinket, and Patch. Record Armor Points, Wounds, and stress (starting at 2).
